title: Trade Policy Activity Index
text:
Trade Policy Activity Index
    
    
    
      A novel composite indicator measuring the evolution of global trade policy
      since the Global Financial Crisis, covering 197 countries and territories.
    
  







  
    About the TPA Index

    
      The Trade Policy Activity (TPA) Index is a novel monthly indicator of global trade
      policy dynamics covering 197 economies since the Global Financial Crisis. It covers
      the period January 2010–October 2025 in the original release, with updated data
      to be made available through this website. Methodological details are available in
      the underlying paper
      (Centorrino et al., 2025).
    

    
      
        How has it been constructed?
        
          The TPA Index is built using a Dynamic Factor Model applied to records of a wide
          range of policy measures — including tariffs, non-tariff measures, and
          subsidies — drawn from two complementary sources: the WTO Trade Monitoring
          Database and the Global Trade Alert. The model treats these records as imperfect
          signals of latent global trade policy activity and extracts a parsimonious global
          trade policy factor capturing their common dynamics. A trend-cycle decomposition
          distinguishes long-term shifts from cyclical fluctuations, while a block structure
          separates the global signal from category-specific variation.
        
      
      
        What does it include?
        
          The dataset provides a headline Trade Policy Activity Index — a monthly
          global measure running from January 2010 (through October 2025 in the original
          release, with periodic updates planned) — together with a set of sub-indices
          by policy category and country group. Separate series track facilitating measures
          and non-facilitating measures, with the latter further split into a restrictive
          subset and a residual composed largely of subsidies. The index is also estimated
          separately for G20 and non-G20 economies, alongside a GDP-weighted variant. All
          series are normalized to mean zero over January 2010–December 2011.
